fields.meta_title: All About Me Questionnaire for Classes and Teams | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build an all about me questionnaire for students, new hires, campers, or mentees, with answers saved to a database you own. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build an All About Me Questionnaire That Gets Read After Day One
fields.hero_description: Build an all about me questionnaire whose answers reach the teacher, manager, or counselor who needs them, in a database you own.
fields.features_subheading: An all about me questionnaire tells someone who a person is before they meet. Emergent builds the app that delivers the answers.
fields.feature_1:
Questions written from who is answering

Describe who answers and who reads the answers, such as third graders and their teacher. Emergent builds the questions and the database behind them, and changes both on request.
fields.feature_2:
One question per screen for children

Turn the questionnaire into a one-question-per-screen flow. A seven-year-old on a classroom tablet sees a single prompt, a few picture choices, and a large Next button.
fields.feature_3:
A roster that shows the whole group at once

Each response is saved as a row in a database you own. Read a class or a mentoring cohort as one roster, then open a single card to see every answer that person gave.
fields.feature_4:
Alerts sent to whoever reads the answers

Get a Slack message or an email each time someone submits. A team lead can read a new hire's answers the hour they come in, without opening a shared folder or searching an inbox.
fields.feature_5:
Every family answers, with no cap

A school with 600 students or a camp running 12 summer sessions sends one questionnaire to all of them. Emergent sets no cap on responses, and late families still get in.
fields.feature_6:
Code that a district or HR team can host

On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository. A school district's IT team can then host the questionnaire on its own servers and keep building on it.

fields.tab_content_1:
By week two, Ms. Ilvane knows who is shy reading aloud

Ms. Ilvane sends the questionnaire home in the first week at Larchmont Creek Elementary, and each third grader answers with a parent. By Friday, 22 of the 24 have come back. Her roster shows that Obadiah learns best by building and is shy reading aloud. His first book report is a model he builds and explains to her.
fields.tab_content_2:
Nadia is introduced to all 40 coworkers on day one

Quarrymoor Analytics sends the questionnaire to each new hire once the offer is signed. Nadia Vosk, a data engineer, answers that she grew up in Tucson, bakes sourdough, and prefers written questions to calls. At 9:00 AM on her first day, the app posts her answers to #team in Slack, where 40 coworkers read them.
fields.tab_content_3:
Elsabet is Betsy to her counselor from the first morning

Cattail Pond Day Camp asks parents to answer the questionnaire for their child before the session. The counselor of the Herons, a group of 14 campers, opens one card per child on her phone at drop-off. Elsabet's card says she goes by Betsy, loves frogs, and brings a stuffed fox named Sprocket that stays in her cubby.
fields.tab_content_4:
Tendai's mentor is the one who also builds robots

Bright Path Mentors asks mentees and volunteer mentors the same questions about interests and goals. The app suggests a pair when two people share 2 or more interests. Tendai, 15, shares robotics, hiking, and sci-fi with Brigida, an engineer. The coordinator approves them, and their first meeting goes on the calendar.

fields.howto_title: How to Make an All About Me Questionnaire
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to make an all about me questionnaire that puts each answer in front of the person who will act on it.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Keep it to about ten questions
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Ask for the name they like first
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Write a version for young children
fields.howto_step_1_des: Start with the reader, not the questions. A teacher planning seats needs different answers than a counselor at drop-off or a coordinator pairing mentors. Write down who opens the answers and what they will do with them in the first week.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Keep the questionnaire short enough to finish in one sitting. About ten questions leave room for a preferred name, a few favorites, how the person likes to learn or work, and one open question. Cut any question nobody will act on.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Put the preferred name at the top. It is the answer the reader uses most, and on a camp card or a class roster it becomes the label for the whole entry. Ask how to say it, too, if names in your group are often misread.
fields.howto_step_4_des: For children who cannot read the questions yet, write a parent version that asks on the child's behalf. For early readers, show one question per screen with picture choices. Keep the words short and put one choice on each screen.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Mark which answers the whole group can see and which only the reader sees. A new hire's hometown can go to the team channel. A student's worries belong with the teacher alone and stay off any shared board.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Send it before the first meeting
fields.howto_step_6_des: Send the questionnaire before the start date, the first week of school, or the camp session. Answers that come in after the first meeting are too late to shape it. Remind anyone who has not answered after a few days.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Describe the questionnaire and where its answers go. Emergent writes the questions and the reader's view, such as a class roster or a post in Slack, on top of a database you own. Ask for any change in plain words.

faq_plan.q: What is an all about me questionnaire?
faq_plan.a: An all about me questionnaire is a short set of questions a person answers about themselves: the name they like, what they enjoy, and how they like to learn or work. Teachers send one at the start of a school year, and managers and camp counselors use it to get to know someone new.

faq_plan.q: How do I create an all about me questionnaire?
faq_plan.a: Decide who will read the answers, then write about ten questions that reader will act on, starting with the person's preferred name. In Emergent's AI form builder, describe the questionnaire and where each answer should go, and it builds the form with a database for every response.

faq_plan.q: What questions go on an all about me questionnaire for students?
faq_plan.a: Ask for the name a student likes, a favorite subject, what they do after school, how they learn best, and one thing they want the teacher to know. Add a question about reading aloud or working in groups if you plan seats or small groups around the answers.

faq_plan.q: How many questions should an all about me questionnaire have?
faq_plan.a: For teens and adults, aim for about ten questions that fit in one sitting. For children in kindergarten or first grade, cut it to five or six and show one question per screen.

faq_plan.q: Can young children answer an all about me questionnaire on their own?
faq_plan.a: Confident readers can, and a layout with one question per screen and picture choices suits early readers. For kindergartners and younger, send a version a parent fills in with the child. Emergent builds both versions from a plain description, with every response saved to the same class roster.

faq_plan.q: What should an all about me questionnaire for new employees ask?
faq_plan.a: Ask where they grew up, a hobby coworkers can ask about, how they like to get questions, and the hours they prefer for meetings. Leave out anything they might not want the team to see, because the answers may be posted where everyone on the team reads them.

faq_plan.q: Should students' all about me questionnaire answers be shared with the class?
faq_plan.a: Share the light answers, such as favorite foods and hobbies, and keep anything about worries, family, or learning needs with the teacher. Mark each question as shared or private before you send it. Every answer sits in a database you own, and you decide which ones appear on a shared board.

faq_plan.q: When should teachers send an all about me questionnaire?
faq_plan.a: Send it before you set the seating chart. Families who get it with the welcome letter in August can answer before the first day of class. A second round in January shows what has changed since the fall.

faq_plan.q: How do I match mentors and mentees with an all about me questionnaire?
faq_plan.a: Ask mentors and mentees about their interests and goals, then pair people whose answers overlap. A rule such as 2 or more shared interests gives the coordinator a short list to approve. Emergent builds that matching rule from a plain description, and the coordinator still signs off on each pair.

faq_plan.q: Can I reuse the same all about me questionnaire every year?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Send the same questions to each new class or group, and keep last year's answers on file next to the new ones. Replace any question that stopped getting useful answers, and add one when your group changes, such as a question about remote work for a team that went hybrid.

plan.angle: The search for all about me questionnaire returns printable worksheets for students and a few lists of icebreaker questions: a sheet that gets filled in once and then sits in a folder. None of them shows the answers being used after week one. This page shows the questionnaire as a small app for four people who need to know someone fast: a third grade teacher reading her class roster, an operations lead whose new hire is introduced in Slack on day one, a day camp counselor meeting campers by nickname, and a mentoring coordinator pairing mentees with mentors by shared interests. The FAQ covers which questions to ask, how many, young children, new hires, privacy and timing.
